{ "source": "{% comment %} Shared review worklist (PP-07, PP-08). Include with: (% include 'OT Review List' reviewtype: 120910200 heading: 'Tax reviews' %) al_reviewtype values are 120910200 Tax and 120910201 AQS. A single al_ReviewInstance carries reviewType rather than separate Tax and AQS tables, so both pages share this template. {% endcomment %} {% comment %} `integer` is the only safe coercion here. `times: 1` repeats a string rather than converting it, so page_number became a string collection and the comparison below threw. `default` cannot rescue that - it only substitutes null. {% endcomment %} {% assign page_size = 25 %} {% assign page_number = request.params['page'] | integer | default: 1 %} {% if page_number < 1 %}{% assign page_number = 1 %}{% endif %} {% comment %} Scope (AD-047, AD-056). `?mine=1` narrows the list to the reviews assigned to the signed-in contact; the bare URL is every review in the discipline. This is what the "Shell stage" notice used to promise and is why that notice is gone. Default is every review, matching the Cases page rather than guessing: a manager landing here sees the discipline's work, and a reviewer is one click from their own. Making "mine" the default would show an empty page to everyone who does not personally hold a review, which reads as a broken list rather than as a scope. Scoping is presentation, never a boundary. Reading another reviewer's work is intended under AD-056; the write boundary is the Contact-anchored table permission chain. Dropped for an anonymous visitor for the reason the case list records: an unguarded {{ user.id }} emits an empty condition value, which matches every row and turns "mine" into "all" silently. {% endcomment %} {% assign f_mine = request.params['mine'] | default: '' %} {% if user == null %}{% assign f_mine = '' %}{% endif %} {% if f_mine != '' and f_mine != '1' %}{% assign f_mine = '' %}{% endif %} {% comment %} Case reference search (project owner, 2026-09-10). Filtered in the query rather than over the rendered rows: this list pages server-side, so a client-side filter would search the page the checker happens to be on and quietly miss the case they were looking for. The condition names the linked case by alias, which is what the case list already does for its outcome filter - and it makes the join behave as an inner one, so a review whose case is missing drops out of a search rather than surviving it as a blank row. {% endcomment %} {% assign f_ref = request.params['ref'] | default: '' %} {% comment %} Review route filter (project owner, 2026-09-10). The routes are read from the environment rather than listed here: al_reviewroute holds three rows whose ids are the environment's own, so hard-coding them would break the moment this ran anywhere but DEV - the same reason DeriveRoute looks a route up by its code instead of by id. The parameter is validated against the ids just fetched, which is this site's rule for anything that reaches FetchXML: an unrecognised value becomes no filter rather than a condition, so nothing typed into the URL is interpolated into the query. {% endcomment %} {% fetchxml routes %} {% endfetchxml %} {% assign f_route = request.params['route'] | default: '' %} {% assign route_ok = false %} {% if f_route != '' %} {% for r in routes.results.entities %} {% if r.al_reviewrouteid == f_route %}{% assign route_ok = true %}{% endif %} {% endfor %} {% endif %} {% unless route_ok %}{% assign f_route = '' %}{% endunless %} {% capture scope_qs %}{% if f_mine == '1' %}mine=1&{% endif %}{% if f_ref != '' %}ref={{ f_ref | url_escape }}&{% endif %}{% if f_route != '' %}route={{ f_route | url_escape }}&{% endif %}{% endcapture %} {% fetchxml reviews %} {% if f_mine == '1' %}{% endif %} {% if f_ref != '' %}{% endif %} {% if f_route != '' %}{% endif %} {% comment %} The route is the case's, so it is read through the case rather than off the review. Outer, because the link above is: a case with no route yet is still a case, and an inner join here would drop its reviews off the list entirely. {% endcomment %} {% endfetchxml %} {% assign rows = reviews.results.entities %} {% comment %} The shared queue (AD-076, extending AD-040, BR-003). Cases sitting at Queued that nobody has picked up, so an AQS checker can take one themselves rather than waiting to be allocated. AQS only (project owner, 2026-09-10). A Tax check is allocated to a named checker by the Tax lead and is never picked up, so the Tax page carries no queue at all and the fetch below is skipped there rather than rendered empty. AD-076 built the button on both pages; this narrows that, it does not reshape it - claiming still writes the same assignment row through the same plug-in. A Tax-then-AQS case still reaches this queue, once its Tax check is submitted: only its AQS leg is ever picked up, and its Tax leg was allocated. Which cases those are is decided by the filter below rather than restated here. Nothing here is a permission boundary. What a checker may actually do is decided by the create permission on al_caseassignment and by ClaimCasePlugin, which re-reads the status and the route server-side (NFR-SEC-01). {% endcomment %} {% assign queued_status = 120910583 %} {% assign is_aqs_queue = false %} {% if reviewtype == 120910201 %}{% assign is_aqs_queue = true %}{% endif %} {% if is_aqs_queue and user %} {% comment %} The queue is readable before it is actionable. Picking a case up depends on ClaimCasePlugin being registered; without it the Web API create still succeeds, because al_name, al_caseassignmentcode, al_assignedon and al_isactive are only *business* required and Dataverse does not enforce that through the API. The page would report success while the case stayed in the queue, leaving assignment rows that AD-037 forbids deleting. So the button is switched on by a site setting, not by deployment. {% endcomment %} {% assign claim_enabled = false %} {% if settings['OutcomeTesting/Claim/Enabled'] == 'true' %}{% assign claim_enabled = true %}{% endif %} {% comment %} Picking a case up needs the AQS reviewer web role: the claim-request contact permission is bound to the Tax and AQS Reviewer roles, and ClaimCasePlugin checks the same role again. A signed-in user without it - a supervisor or an adviser reading the queue, now that page.reviews reaches them - used to be offered "Run checks" and answered with a 403 read as "you may not have permission". The server stays the boundary (NFR-SEC-01); this only stops the page offering an action it knows will be refused, and says why instead. {% endcomment %} {% assign claim_role = 'AL Portal - AQS Reviewer' %} {% assign can_claim = false %} {% if claim_enabled and user.roles contains claim_role %}{% assign can_claim = true %}{% endif %} {% fetchxml available %} {% comment %} Whether a Tax-then-AQS case has reached its AQS leg, decided by what it still owes rather than by the route alone. This queue used to ask the route for al_requirestaxreview ne 1, which excluded a Tax-then-AQS case from it permanently - before its Tax check and, the reason this changed, after it too. A passed Tax check returns the case to Queued (OutcomeRules .NextCaseStatusForTax; HopsFor skips the Submitted hop precisely because the case is not submitted, only its Tax review is), and the case then sat in a queue no AQS checker could see. The test is a *submitted* Tax review, not an open one. A queued case that nobody has claimed has no review instance at all - ClaimCasePlugin creates it - so "no open Tax review" is equally true before the Tax check and after it, and keying on that would have put fresh Tax-then-AQS cases straight onto this queue and broken BR-004's ordering. "A Tax review has been submitted" separates the two states. Here - the route requires AQS, and either it never required Tax or the Tax review is in. BR-004's ordering is then enforced by the data rather than restated here. An outer link asserted null on its alias is FetchXML's "no such row exists"; the OR across two aliases is the same shape the case list uses for its outcome filter. Nothing here is a boundary. ClaimCasePlugin re-reads the status and the route server-side and refuses a claim this list should not have offered (NFR-SEC-01). {% endcomment %} {% endfetchxml %} {% assign unassigned = available.results.entities %}

The old reason: al_checkername was the "Checker name" column of the upload file as much as it was the allocated checker, so a queued case nobody had been given still carried a person's name, and printing it under a caption promising "no checker" made unclaimed cases read as somebody else's work. The import stopped writing that column on 2026-09-14, and the column itself is now dormant. The reason now: the case carries al_taxcheckername and al_aqscheckername, each stamped by the allocation of that review. A case in THIS list is one nobody has claimed, so the column for the discipline being claimed is empty by definition - it would be a column of blanks. What decides that a case is available is its status and the absence of a claim, which is what the filter above asks. The two names are shown on the case record, where the allocation they describe belongs. {% endcomment %} {% if can_claim %}{% endif %} {% for c in unassigned %} {% if can_claim %} {% endif %} {% endfor %}
